memories.author: D03
memories.text:
36‑year‑old female electrician reviewed for epilepsy and newly diagnosed iron‑deficiency anaemia.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports occasional mild fatigue and no recent seizures; medication adherence is good.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 55 kg, height 1.55 m, BMI 22.9 (normal). No pallor, neurologic exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Epilepsy on levetiracetam and lamotrigine; iron‑deficiency anaemia likely due to dietary insufficiency.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start levetiracetam 500 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD, ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD. Check CBC, ferritin, MCV, serum sodium, creatinine in 4 weeks. Return if seizure activity increases, fever >39°C, chest pain, breathlessness, or blood in stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Levetiracetam 500 mg BD; Lamotrigine 50 mg BD; Ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Levetiracetam 500 mg BD; Lamotrigine 50 mg BD; Ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD plus 200 mg on alternate days.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: EEG performed to assess seizure burden. Background activity normal, no epileptiform discharges observed. No focal slowing. Interpretation: No electrographic evidence of seizure focus; epilepsy clinically controlled on current regimen.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
36‑year‑old female electrician for routine follow‑up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Denies seizures since last visit; reports mild fatigue improving with iron therapy.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/78 mmHg, weight 56 kg, BMI 23.3 (overweight). No pallor, neurologically normal.
IMPRESSION: Epilepsy stable; iron‑deficiency anaemia responding, Hb rising.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Advise balanced diet rich in iron, reduce refined carbs, increase aerobic activity 150 min/week. Repeat CBC, ferritin, MCV in 8 weeks. Return if seizure, fever >39°C, chest pain, breathlessness, or blood in stools.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I had a brief jerking episode of my left arm lasting about 20 seconds yesterday morning while at work. I did not lose consciousness but felt confused for a few minutes afterwards. I am worried my seizure medicine may not be enough.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
36‑year‑old female electrician after breakthrough seizure.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Reports a focal arm jerking episode with post‑ictal confusion, no loss of consciousness.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/77 mmHg, weight 56 kg, BMI 23.3, neurologically normal.
IMPRESSION: Possible breakthrough seizure on levetiracetam; consider dose optimisation.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase levetiracetam to 750 mg BD. Counsel on seizure precautions, sleep hygiene, avoid triggers. Repeat serum creatinine in 4 weeks. Return if seizure frequency increases, prolonged post‑ictal state, fever >39°C, chest pain, breathlessness, or blood in stools.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Levetiracetam 750 mg BD; Lamotrigine 75 mg BD; Ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD plus 200 mg on alternate days.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
36‑year‑old female electrician for annual review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Denies seizures in past 6 months; reports good energy, no fatigue.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 57 kg, BMI 23.7 (overweight). No pallor, neurologic exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Epilepsy well controlled on levetiracetam 750 mg BD and lamotrigine 75 mg BD. Iron‑deficiency anaemia improved, Hb approaching normal.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Order fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar. Advise maintain iron‑rich diet, limit saturated fats, aim for 150 min/week moderate exercise. Influenza vaccine offered; patient declined. Return if seizure, fever >39°C, chest pain, breathlessness, or blood in stools.
